<h>Invitatorium</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, * Exsultémus Dómino.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, * Exsultémus Dómino.
<c>I</c>ubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem ejus in confessióne, et in psalmis jubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, * Exsultémus Dómino.
<c>Q</c>uóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu ejus sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Exsultémus Dómino.
<c>Q</c>uóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus ejus <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus ejus, et oves páscuæ ejus.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, * Exsultémus Dómino.
<c>H</c>ódie, si vocem ejus audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Exsultémus Dómino.
<c>Q</c>uadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus jurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, * Exsultémus Dómino.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Exsultémus Dómino.

<h>Invitatory</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Come * Let us glorify the Lord.
<r>Ant.</r> Come * Let us glorify the Lord.
<c>L</c>et us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
<r>Ant.</r> Come * Let us glorify the Lord.
<c>F</c>or the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.
<r>Ant.</r> Let us glorify the Lord.
<c>F</c>or the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. <n>(genuflect)</n> Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
<r>Ant.</r> Come * Let us glorify the Lord.
<c>T</c>oday if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
<r>Ant.</r> Let us glorify the Lord.
<c>F</c>orty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.
<r>Ant.</r> Come * Let us glorify the Lord.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

<r>Dan 7:1-3</r>
<n>1</n> Anno primo Baltássar regis Babylónis, Dániel sómnium vidit: vísio autem cápitis ejus in cubíli suo: et sómnium scribens, brevi sermóne comprehéndit: summatímque perstríngens, ait:
<n>2</n> Vidébam in visióne mea nocte: et ecce quátuor venti cæli pugnábant in mari magno.
<n>3</n> Et quátuor béstiæ grandes ascendébant de mari divérsæ inter se.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

* Et ea, quæ sub ipso erant, replébant templum.

<r>Commemoratio Ss. Quatuor Coronatorum Martyrum</r>
<r>Ant.</r> Isti sunt Sancti, qui pro Dei amóre minas hóminum contempsérunt: sancti Mártyres in regno cælórum exsúltant cum Angelis. O quam pretiósa est mors Sanctórum, qui assídue assístunt ante Dóminum, et ab ínvicem non sunt separáti!

<r>Ant.</r> These are the holy ones who for the love of Christ, recked nothing of the threats of men. In the kingdom of heaven the holy martyrs are filled with joy in the company of Angels. b.1c6374ae9c:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>Q</c>uinto Idus Novémbris Luna décima. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>R</h>omæ, in Lateráno, Dedicátio Basílicæ sanctíssimi Salvatóris, quæ ómnium Urbis et Orbis Ecclesiárum est mater et caput.
<h>A</h>maséæ, in Ponto, natális sancti Theodóri mílitis, qui, témpore Maximiáni Imperatóris, pro Christiánæ fídei confessióne, fórtiter cæsus et in cárcerem missus; deínde, Dómino sibi apparénte ac monénte ut constánter et viríliter ágeret, relevátus est; novíssime, postquam in equúleo suspénsus et úngulis ita excarnificátus est, ut ejus interióra apparérent nuda, ardéntibus ígnibus comburéndus tráditur. Ipsíus vero laudes sanctus Gregórius Nyssénus præcláro encómio celebrávit.
<h>T</h>yánæ, in Cappadócia, pássio sancti Oréstis, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre.
<h>T</h>hessalonícæ sancti Alexándri Mártyris, sub Maximiáno Príncipe.
<h>A</h>pud Bitúricas, in Aquitánia, sancti Ursíni Confessóris, qui, Romæ ordinátus a successóribus Apostolórum, primus eídem Bituricénsi urbi destinátur Epíscopus.
<h>N</h>eápoli, in Campánia, sancti Agrippíni Epíscopi, miráculis clari.
<h>C</h>onstantinópoli sanctárum Vírginum Eustóliæ Románæ, et Sópatræ, fíliæ Maurítii Imperatóris.
<h>B</h>erýti, in Sýria, commemorátio Imáginis Salvatóris, quæ, a Judǽis crucifíxa, tam copiósum emísit sánguinem, ut Orientáles et Occidentáles Ecclésiæ ex eo ubértim accéperint.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.0db981a762:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>N</c>ovember 9th 2027, the 10th day of the Moon,
<h>O</h>n the morrow is kept the feast of the Dedication of the Cathedral Church of the Saviour at Rome, (in the year 324).
<h>U</h>pon the same 9th day of November, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Amasea, in Pontus, the holy soldier Theodore. In the time of the Emperor Maximian he was heavily flogged and cast into prison for his profession of the Christian faith, in prison the Lord appeared unto him, and bade him be steadfast and do manfully, then he was taken out and stretched upon the rack and torn with hooks until his inner parts were seen, and lastly he was thrown into the fire. Holy Gregory of Nyssa hath told his praises in a noble discourse.
<h>A</h>t Tyana, in Cappadocia, under the Emperor Diocletian, the holy martyr Orestes.
<h>A</h>t Thessalonica, under the Emperor Maximian, the holy martyr Alexander.
<h>A</h>t Bourges, the holy Confessor Ursinus, who was ordained at Rome by the successors of the Apostles, and sent to that city as the first Bishop thereof.
<h>A</h>t Naples, in Campania, holy Agrippinus, Bishop (of that see,) famous for miracles.
<h>A</h>t Constantinople, the holy Virgins Eustolia of Rome, and Sopatra, daughter of the Emperor Maurice.
<h>A</h>t Beirut, in Lebanon, is made commemoration of an image of the Saviour which was crucified by the Jews, (about the year 765,) and so much Blood flowed therefrom, that the Churches both of the East and West have plentifully received thereof.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.

b.a440500b33:
<h>Prayer</h>
<c>L</c>ord have mercy upon us, Christ have mercy upon us, Lord have mercy upon us.
<n><k>Our Father</k> is said silently until <k>And lead us not into temptation:</k>.</n>
<c>O</c>ur Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.
<r>℣.</r> And lead us not into temptation:
<r>℟.</r> But deliver us from evil.

<r>℣.</r> The Lord be with you.
<r>℟.</r> And with thy spirit.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> Lord, we beseech thee to keep thy family continually in godliness, that they who do lean only upon the hope of thine heavenly grace, may evermore be defended by thy mighty power.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Commemoratio Ss. Quatuor Coronatorum Martyrum</r>
<r>Ant.</r> Isti sunt Sancti, qui pro Dei amóre minas hóminum contempsérunt: sancti Mártyres in regno cælórum exsúltant cum Angelis. O quam pretiósa est mors Sanctórum, qui assídue assístunt ante Dóminum, et ab ínvicem non sunt separáti!

<r>℣.</r> Mirábilis Deus.
<r>℟.</r> In sanctis suis.

<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>P</c>ræsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui gloriósos Mártyres fortes in sua confessióne cognóvimus, pios apud te in nostra intercessióne sentiámus.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Commemoration of Four Crowned Martyrs</r>
<r>Ant.</r> These are the holy ones who for the love of Christ, recked nothing of the threats of men. In the kingdom of heaven the holy martyrs are filled with joy in the company of Angels. O how precious in the sight of the Lord was the death of these His saints who now stand day and night in His presence and are not divided the one from the other.

<r>℣.</r> Mirábilis Deus.
<r>℟.</r> In sanctis suis.

<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>G</c>rant, we beseech thee, O Almighty God, that we who know thy glorious witnesses to have been in their testifying leal toward thee, may feel, now that they are with thee, that they are in their prayers pitiful towards us.
